question: Could the human reference transcriptions have been in the models' training data?
method: For each of the ten DECODE records: the record page was read with a logged-in session (stored cookie) and its 'Access Mode' field noted; the reference transcription file was requested from de-crypt.org/decrypt-custom/filesrv/ without any cookie, and one file (R7) was requested with the cookie.
anonymous_request: all ten files: HTTP 200 but the body is DECODE's 17,947-byte forbidden.png placeholder, not the text
conclusion: The reference transcriptions are not served to anonymous clients, so an ordinary web crawl would not have collected them. This lowers the contamination risk; it does not rule it out (registered users can download them, and parts of some documents may be quoted in print or online).
page_images: The page images were not checked here; some DECODE records serve images publicly. Images alone carry no transcription.
